joy and weeping in the geulah

title.en: Twelve paths now, seven in the future

summary.en: The Rav opens with the Midrash on 'Hashem Yimloch' and the twelve paths in the sea, notes that in the future the sea will split again into seven channels, and asks why. He brings the Midrash that the names of the Shvatim allude to the geulah, with Yosef standing for 'Yosif Hashem shenis yado'.

title.en: The sea's condition and its refusal

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that the sea refused to split until it saw Yosef's coffin, because Yosef fled from Potiphar's wife. He asks why it refused if Hashem had made a condition with it at creation, and asks why Rashi's mention of the condition comes only after the sea returned to its place.

title.en: A half geulah, like Yachatz

summary.en: The Rav brings the Rama MiPano that Klal Yisrael left Mitzrayim after 210 years instead of 400, and the Chida that this is why the matzah is broken at Yachatz. He answers that the sea refused because the time of full joy had not come, and split only when Yosef's coffin showed it there would be a second splitting.

title.en: Shabbos Shirah: the inner side of music

summary.en: For Shabbos Shirah the Rav turns to music: Moshe Rabbeinu was taught it and taught the Leviim, and musicians know its science but not its inner meaning. He explains the seven notes and the octave, and that harmony is pleasant like a good shidduch while clashing sounds irritate.

title.en: Music as a key to Torah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gra, through the Pe'as HaShulchan, that the secrets of Torah require the wisdom of music, and the Tikkunei Zohar that some heavenly chambers open only through niggun, which is why piano keys are called keys. He tells the Chabad tradition that the Ba'al HaTanya answered the scholars of Shklov with a niggun.

title.en: The sevens of creation and Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem created seven days with seven middos, and brings Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer that of every seven the seventh is chosen. The seven notes correspond to all these sevens; only with the seventh is the harp complete, which is Shabbos, and David, the seventh of the Ushpizin, ends Tehillim with ten instruments and gave the seven voices of Mizmor l'David.

title.en: Seven is unity; music is a shidduch

summary.en: The Rav contrasts the seven Ushpizin, who are unity and culminate in David, with the twelve Nesi'im, who are division. Creation is harmonious and beautiful like music, a shidduch made in Heaven, while today's music is noise without harmony that stirs up lust.

title.en: Black keys, white keys and the twelve paths

summary.en: The Rav explains the five black keys as broken half-notes, like the shevarim of the shofar: white keys alone make a joyful niggun and black keys alone a sad one. With the passuk 'bakosharos' read as weeping and song, he answers that the sea split into twelve, seven white and five black, because the geulah from Mitzrayim was joy mixed with weeping.

title.en: Seven paths and an eighth string

summary.en: The Rav explains that when Moshiach comes there will be only joy, so the sea will split into seven; to the question how music can exist without the black notes he brings the Gemara that the harp will then have eight strings. This also explains why they said 'Yimloch', and why the sea's condition is mentioned after it returned: it still owes the second splitting.

title.en: Tu B'Shvat: the union called Ilan

summary.en: After reporting that day's news of bombs in Meah She'arim with one person lightly hurt, the Rav explains Tu B'Shvat as the day of the Ilan: Hashem's written name joined with the name as it is read is the union of Hashem and Knesses Yisrael, equal in gematria to 'ilan'. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar and the Chiddushei HaRim that new Torah comes down from this day.

title.en: A flow of chesed: use the keys

summary.en: The Rav brings the Sanzer Rav that from Tu B'Shvat until Shavuos every two weeks brings a special day, a continuous flow of chesed, and urges learning, davening, tzedakah and good middos now. He brings the Zohar on saying Shiras HaYam daily, the passuk 'Adam bikar', and closes with the trees' awakening and the tenth, future song of eight notes.

catalogTitle: מדארף אפהיטן די מויל!! אזוי בויעט מען די ביהמ"ק!! דרשה לילדי תפארת יונה

oneLiner.en: Speaking to children after Pesach, the Rav teaches that guarding the mouth, both what enters it and what leaves it, keeps the healing of the matzah and lets every Jewish child help finish the Beis HaMikdash through small, hidden acts.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with matzah as the medicine of emunah: after Pesach the cure must be kept by not eating 'poison'. Parshas Shemini teaches care for what enters the mouth, Tazria-Metzora for what leaves it, for the mouth is a two-way street. A clean mouth makes tefillah accepted; the Jewish mouth is a mizbeach, so one must be strict with hechsherim. One who does what he can is protected from what he cannot, as stories of the Beis HaLevi and the Yeshuos Yaakov show. In Iyar Shlomo began building the Beis HaMikdash; every perfect mitzvah adds a piece to the heavenly Beis HaMikdash, and the Divrei Chaim's paroches story shows that sins tear it down. The great tzaddikim built the big parts; what is left are small touches, like refusing doubtful candy, holding back a shaming joke and guarding the eyes, and Moshiach will point to the child who finished them.

en: Matzah is a medicine of emunah, and after Pesach the healing must be kept by guarding what one eats.
The mouth is a two-way street: Shemini teaches care for what goes in, Tazria-Metzora for what comes out.
Tefillah depends on the mouth: Hashem accepts the tefillah of a mouth that is kept holy, since the Jewish mouth is a mizbeach.
Whoever guards himself as far as he can is protected by Hashem from what he cannot control.
Every complete mitzvah goes up to heaven and becomes a piece of the Beis HaMikdash, while sins tear it down.
The great parts of the Beis HaMikdash are already built; what remains are small touches that even small people of this generation can do.
One becomes an ehrlicher Yid not through the big mitzvos everyone does, but through a hundred small, hidden acts of self-restraint.

candidateTopics: chodesh Iyar and preparing for Shavuos

title.en: Matzah's cure and the two-way mouth

summary.en: The Rav calls matzah a medicine of emunah and says that after Pesach the cure must be kept by not eating forbidden food. He links Parshas Shemini to what enters the mouth and Tazria-Metzora, where the metzora is a motzi shem ra, to what leaves it.

title.en: A holy mouth, an accepted tefillah

summary.en: Every child needs yeshuos, and the Rav explains that tefillah comes through the mouth, so Hashem accepts it from a mouth kept holy. He urges care with hechsherim and doubtful ingredients, asking the rebbi and parents, because the Jewish mouth is a mizbeach.

title.en: Raglei chasidav yishmor: the Beis HaLevi's chicken

summary.en: The Rav asks how one can guard against a mistake one cannot help, and answers with the passuk that Hashem guards the feet of His pious ones. He tells how the Beis HaLevi, given chicken for the road by Rabbi Yehoshua Leib Diskin's household, left it uneaten when it turned out to have a shailah.

title.en: The guarding malach and the Yeshuos Yaakov

summary.en: Each time a child says 'I don't eat that', a holy malach is created that goes with him and saves him from mistakes. The Rav tells how the Yeshuos Yaakov, a guest at a local Rav, got caught up in a Rambam and never ate the pancake that had been fried in a fleishig pan.

title.en: Iyar: preparing for Shavuos, building the Mikdash

summary.en: In Iyar Shlomo HaMelech began building the Beis HaMikdash, and the Rav explains that what the Torah dates returns every year. As at Sinai, the heavens come down each Shavuos, and how one prepares in sefirah, with a holy mouth for Torah, decides what Shavuos one has; Iyar is the time to build the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: Mitzvos build, sins tear: the Divrei Chaim's paroches

summary.en: The Rav explains that the third Beis HaMikdash will come down built from above, and every perfect mitzvah becomes material for it in heaven. He tells that the Divrei Chaim said only the paroches was missing, and that he had made it but a great rasha tore it; tzaddikim build and reshaim destroy.

title.en: Only the small touches are missing

summary.en: The builders will win the race, and when the Beis HaMikdash is complete Moshiach will come. The Rav says earlier tzaddikim already made the big parts; unlike a simple man moving into an unfinished house, the King of Glory needs it perfect, so a handle must be polished and a window cleaned. Refusing a doubtful candy at a cousin's, trivial for great tzaddikim, is a real test for a child and builds the Mikdash.

title.en: The held-back joke and silence in shul

summary.en: The Rav describes a boy who holds back a clever joke that would shame a friend, avoids idle talk with his chavrusa, and refuses to answer a friend during chazaras hashatz. Such hidden restraint polishes the Beis HaMikdash; he ties it to the metzora who must keep his mouth covered and to the beis knesses as a place of kedushah.

title.en: Small things make an ehrlicher Yid; Moshiach points to the boy

summary.en: The Rav says one need not do great feats like the tzaddikim; big mitzvos like shofar, megillah and tefillin everyone does, while a hundred small things, like guarding the eyes in the street, make an ehrlicher Yid. He closes picturing Moshiach at the great seudah pointing to the boy whose shemiras hapeh and shemiras einayim finished the Beis HaMikdash, with a brachah.

catalogTitle: ביאור הפטורה - אליהו יתקן נשמות ישראל אפ' הרחוקים ביותר (מצורעים שבדמשק) (פסח)

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Eliyahu HaNavi's task is to rectify even the most distant Jewish souls, the 'metzora'im of Damascus' like Gechazi, until Damascus itself becomes Jerusalem, and that Pesach is Eliyahu's time.

abstract.en: Opening from the haftarah of Shabbos HaGadol, the Rav asks what Eliyahu's task is. He brings the Pri Tzaddik that Eliyahu needed atonement for his offering outside the Mikdash on Mount Carmel and was sent to Damascus, and the Noam Elimelech that a tzaddik must descend to raise the fallen. He then turns to Gechazi, who has no share in the World to Come because his tzaraas never leaves him and a metzora may not enter Jerusalem, and whom Elisha sought in Damascus. Building on the Midrash that Jerusalem will spread until Damascus, the Rav explains that Eliyahu, a soul of the rectified world, never sinned: Carmel will be inside Jerusalem, and Damascus, root of incurable tzaraas, will become Mikdash. Eliyahu will answer every 'teiku' and bring Gechazi in. He ends with the generation's tzaraas, loshon hara and pritzus, and how to prepare for Pesach.

en: Shabbos HaGadol and all of Pesach carry the influence of Eliyahu HaNavi, who comes to every Jewish seder.
A tzaddik must sometimes descend from his level, sharing a trace of the fallen one's flaw, in order to lift him up.
Gechazi has no share in the World to Come according to the Mishnah because his tzaraas is permanent and a metzora cannot enter Jerusalem, which corresponds to the World to Come.
Eliyahu is a soul of the rectified world; Mount Carmel will be inside the future Jerusalem, so his offering there was never truly 'outside'.
Damascus, the root of incurable tzaraas, will become Mikdash when Jerusalem spreads to it, and the souls cast out there will have a tikun.
Eliyahu will answer the 'teiku' questions because he will answer the questions on the questioned Jews, bringing even Gechazi into the camp of Israel.
To greet Eliyahu on Pesach one must cleanse the two parts of the bris, the mouth and the body, from loshon hara, machlokes and pritzus.

candidateTopics: offering outside the Mikdash on Mount Carmel

title.en: Shabbos HaGadol, the Shabbos of Eliyahu

summary.en: The Rav opens with the haftarah of Shabbos HaGadol, which ends with the promise to send Eliyahu, and asks what Eliyahu's essence and task are. He brings two hints of Eliyahu in this week's parsha heard in the name of the first Belzer Rav.

title.en: Eliyahu's offering on Carmel and the flight to Damascus

summary.en: From the prohibition of offerings outside the Mikdash, the Rav brings the Pri Tzaddik that Eliyahu, though he offered on Carmel by a prophet's word, needed atonement and was sent to Damascus. He then asks why specifically Eliyahu will resolve all the 'teiku' questions of the Gemara.

title.en: A tzaddik descends to raise the fallen

summary.en: The Rav brings the Noam Elimelech's parable of a man on a roof who must climb down to lift someone fallen in a pit: only one who shares a trace of the flaw can raise the sinner. He shows this in the Midrash on Moshe breaking the luchos after the eigel.

title.en: Gechazi and his share in the World to Come

summary.en: The Rav tells how Elisha cursed Gechazi with Naaman's tzaraas forever and brings the Mishnah that Gechazi has no share in the World to Come. He explains with the Pri Tzaddik that a permanent metzora can never enter Jerusalem, and contrasts the dorshei reshumos, who hold that all those listed do have a share.

title.en: Two readings: 'Elisha went' and 'Elisha came'

summary.en: The Rav notes that the Gemara quotes 'Elisha went to Damascus' while the Tanach reads 'Elisha came'. He suggests both versions are true, like differing Torah spellings, and that 'went' without arriving matches the Mishnah while 'came' matches the dorshei reshumos.

title.en: An offering outside for those cast outside

summary.en: The Rav explains that idol worshippers, like the tribe of Dan, are pushed outside the camp, and that Eliyahu had to bring an offering 'outside' to open a door for Jews who were outside. Atonement for this meant leaving Eretz Yisroel, and he asks why the destination had to be Damascus.

title.en: Eliyahu, a soul of the rectified world

summary.en: The Rav says Eliyahu really needed no atonement: his soul is from before the sin of the Tree of Knowledge and lives in the rectified world. He uses this to answer Tosfos's question on the Gemara where Eliyahu, a kohen, stood in a cemetery: in the future the halacha will follow Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the Shabbos soul.

title.en: Damascus, root of Naaman's tzaraas

summary.en: From the Midrash that Jerusalem will spread to Damascus, the Rav explains that Carmel will be in Jerusalem, so for Eliyahu it was not 'outside'. Damascus is the opposite of Jerusalem, the root of the non-Jewish tzaraas of Naaman; that tzaraas passed to Gechazi and drew him to Damascus, which is how Chazal knew where Elisha went, and in the future Jerusalem will come to the metzora.

title.en: From Damesek will come Mikdash

summary.en: The Rav brings the Yalkut that Jerusalem will be built on four mountains including Carmel, and that Mikdash and Damesek share letters. Eliyahu gathered the Baal worshippers on Carmel and called them to teshuvah now, and Hashem's command to flee to Damascus only looked like exile; Eliyahu knew Damascus is Jerusalem.

title.en: Darmesek with a reish in Divrei Hayamim

summary.en: The Rav asks why Divrei Hayamim alone spells Damascus with an added reish. He explains that Divrei Hayamim, the last of the twenty-four books, is the completion of malchus, that reish stands for shalom, the opposite of tzaraas, and that Damascus with the reish equals 'machaneh Yisroel' in gematria.

title.en: Elisha, Gechazi and the herald of good

summary.en: The Rav explains that Elisha continues Eliyahu's work, and that the fifth cup, Eliyahu's cup, equals Damesek in gematria. He brings a teaching that the complete revelation of Eliyahu comes with Elisha and then Gechazi running after them, and that 'mevaser tov' equals Eliyahu, Elisha and Gechazi; even the people of Sedom are Jewish souls who will reach the World to Come.

title.en: Questioned Jews and the answers of Eliyahu

summary.en: The Rav explains that every kushya is a klipah and every Jew is a letter in the Torah; a 'teiku' in the Gemara reflects a questioned Jew at the root of that halacha. Eliyahu will answer the questions on the Jews and so answer the Torah's questions, bringing Gechazi into the camp, and as angel of the bris he frees Jews from tzaraas, also at the seder.

title.en: A time of Gechazi in this generation

summary.en: Using the Sefer Yetzirah's place, time and soul, the Rav pairs Jerusalem, Eliyahu and Pesach against Damascus, Gechazi and a time of Gechazi. He describes his generation as one of tzaraas, pritzus, loshon hara and machlokes, with the Satan bringing impurity into homes before Moshiach's coming, and says that against this comes the time of Eliyahu, Pesach.

title.en: The bris of the mouth and telling the wonders

summary.en: The Rav brings Rebbe Reb Bunim that Eliyahu composed the Haggadah, and explains that Eliyahu's matter is the holiness of the bris, both the bris of the body and the bris of the tongue. He brings a Midrash that the Shunamis was brought back so that Gechazi would not tell Elisha's wonders, and concludes that one must purify the mouth to tell Hashem's wonders and pass on the mesorah at the seder.

title.en: The oxen at the market, and the closing wish

summary.en: The Rav tells how Rabbi Yitzchak of Skver sent his son to find Eliyahu in the street, and the son learned from the calm and the straining oxen that a good thought is itself from Eliyahu. He closes with the Belzer Rav's hint again and the wish that Eliyahu come with Elisha and Gechazi together, when Damascus will reach Jerusalem.

catalogTitle: אהרן והכהנים הם בחינת מדת הוד - קודש הקדשים - בחינת רשב"י

oneLiner.en: Starting from the Gemara on making a brachah over a whole loaf, the Rav explains that Hashem's Name rests only on shleimus, that every Jew is bound to Olam Haba, Shabbos and Eretz Yisrael, and that the weeks of Sefirah are the work of becoming whole before Shavuos.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Gemara in Berachos on whether to make the brachah over a broken piece or a whole loaf. He explains that a brachah is said over the more important food because it awakens more gratitude, but the advantage of a whole loaf is different: from the blemished kohen in this week's parsha he shows that Hashem's Name, Shalom, rests only on what is whole. He then turns to the custom of saying 'Kol Yisrael yesh lahem chelek le'olam haba' before Pirkei Avos and, following the Maharal, explains that every Jewish soul comes from Olam Haba and must return there; Shabbos, Torah, Eretz Yisrael and Olam Haba are one root, and Jews have mitzvos because of that bond, not the reverse. Through the Chozeh of Lublin he presents the seven weeks of Sefirah as conquering the seven nations, the seven middos, within oneself. He closes with the shleimus of the kohanim, the shedim created without it, and the call to reach temimus by Shavuos.

en: The brachah goes over the more important food because holding it in hand awakens a greater feeling of thanks to Hashem.
Hashem's Name is Shalom and rests only on what is whole, which is why a blemished kohen or korban is unfit for the avodah.
Every Jew must eventually reach Olam Haba, because every Jewish soul comes from there; mitzvos and sins only make the road easier or harder.
Shabbos, Torah, Eretz Yisrael and Olam Haba are one thing, and the Jewish people is rooted in all of them.
A Jew is Hashem's child and can never stop being His child; sins bring punishment but do not undo the relationship.
The days of Sefirah are days of battle, in which a Jew must prepare himself for Shavuos by refining his seven middos.

Shabbos as a taste of Olam Haba
Rashi on why the Torah begins with Bereishis

title.en: A piece or a whole loaf for the brachah

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara in Berachos on whether to make hamotzi over the larger broken pieces or over the whole loaf, with Rashi's and Tosafos's readings and Rabbi Yochanan's statement that a whole loaf is the choicest mitzvah. He asks why Rabbi Yochanan phrases it differently, and brings the conclusion that a yerei shamayim fulfills both.

title.en: Gratitude, and what is special about wholeness

summary.en: The Rav explains that the brachah is made over the most important food because it arouses more gratitude, and asks what advantage a whole loaf has, since it is not tastier. He answers from the blemished kohen in the parsha: Hashem's Name, Shalom, rests only on wholeness.

title.en: Rav Huna and Rabbi Yochanan: two considerations

summary.en: The Rav distinguishes the material advantage that awakens gratitude from the spiritual advantage of wholeness where Hashem's Name rests, a lesson learned from the avodah of korbanos. Rav Huna weighs gratitude, while Rabbi Yochanan introduces a different consideration, which explains his wording.

title.en: Kol Yisrael before Pirkei Avos

summary.en: The Rav turns to the custom of saying the Mishnah 'Kol Yisrael yesh lahem chelek le'olam haba' before each perek of Pirkei Avos. Following the Maharal, he explains that it comes after the chapters on those liable to death to teach that every Jew must reach Olam Haba, since his soul comes from there, and that it is learned on Shabbos because Shabbos, Torah and Olam Haba are one.

title.en: Shabbos, Eretz Yisrael, Yom Kippur and Yovel

summary.en: The Rav explains that Jewish souls, Shabbos and Torah are all hewn from Olam Haba, and that just as there are Jewish and non-Jewish days, Eretz Yisrael is the Jewish land, corresponding to Eretz Yisrael above, and so it too keeps Shabbos. Shabbos has its own Shabbos in Yom Kippur, and the land in Yovel, when each returns to his source, as every Jew returns to Olam Haba.

title.en: Why the Torah begins with Bereishis

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that Torah, Eretz Yisrael and Olam Haba are given through suffering, and Rashi's question why the Torah does not begin with the first mitzvah. Through Avraham's question how he would know his children would keep the land, answered with korbanos, and the creation of man from the place of the mizbeach, he explains that the word Bereishis hints at Yisrael, Torah and Shabbos, and that Jews have mitzvos because of their bond, not the reverse.

title.en: Netzer mata'ai: Hashem's planting and His child

summary.en: Returning to the Mishnah's verse, the Rav explains 'le'olam yirshu aretz': the Jews are a plant that Hashem Himself planted and that can grow only on its own soil, Eretz Yisrael. A Jew is a son to Hashem and can never stop being one; Hashem boasts of every Jew, even the lowest.

title.en: The seven nations and the seven weeks of Sefirah

summary.en: The Rav asks how the Jews acquired Eretz Yisrael and answers: by conquering the seven nations. He brings the Chozeh of Lublin that the seven nations are the seven middos, and explains the seven weeks of Sefirah as the work of conquering them within oneself, week by week, until every day becomes Shabbos; he connects this to the psalm Lamenatze'ach said during Sefirah.

title.en: Sefirah as days of battle and preparation

summary.en: The Rav describes the days of Sefirah as days of battle and of din, and points out that for no other Yom Tov does the Torah command a preparation as it does before Shavuos. Shavuos is the fiftieth day, like the place of the Mikdash itself, and Eretz Yisrael is the preparation for Har Habayis.

title.en: Why the shedim were left without bodies

summary.en: The Rav brings the teaching that the shedim were created on Erev Shabbos just before Shabbos and were left without bodies, and explains that this is not lack of time but their nature: they were made incomplete so that they could have no connection to Shabbos, which is shleimus.

title.en: The kohanim, the Kohen Gadol and the Kodesh HaKodashim

summary.en: Turning to the parsha, the Rav explains that the kohanim, sons of Aharon, are a 'small Shabbos' and the Kohen Gadol, who enters the Kodesh HaKodashim, a great Shabbos. His special laws, the blemished kohen and the blemished korban all express that the avodah requires shleimus.

title.en: The moadim, 'temimos', and the blasphemer

summary.en: The Rav notes that the parsha of the moadim opens with Shabbos, which is shleimus, and that the Sefirah weeks must be 'temimos', whole. He connects this to Rabbi Akiva's students and to the one who 'pierced' Hashem's Name, which is shalom and shleimus, and says every Jew must come to Shavuos in full temimus.

title.en: The Jewish soul as a korban without blemish

summary.en: The Rav closes with the teaching that Michael brings the souls of Jews before Hashem as korbanos, so the soul, like a korban, must be whole. The Sefirah days are hard and are a battle; one must love Hashem, Torah and every Jew and give all seven middos over to Hashem, to reach temimus.

catalogTitle: A Lesson from יתרו - It's Never too Late

oneLiner.en: The Rav shows from Yisro, from the latecomers of Kriyas Yam Suf and Amalek, and from the Haftarah of Yeshaya that Hashem draws every Jew close and that it is never too late to come to the Torah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with 'va'avi eschem eilai' and the Ahavah Rabbah blessing: Hashem has declared that He wants us close. The theme of the sedra lies in its name: Yisro, the convert who was brought close, asked Moshe to come out to him because he needed courage. Rashi says Yisro heard of Kriyas Yam Suf and the war of Amalek. The Rav reconciles the Targum, which calls the nechshalim latecomers, with Rashi, who says the cloud expelled them: their own tardiness put them outside, and Hashem's anger at Amalek for attacking them still burns. Dasan and Aviram, too, came late and received a private splitting of the sea. From these Yisro learned that a latecomer is welcome. Shavuos is Matan Torah for the prepared; Parshas Yisro is a rerun for latecomers, an awakening from above, as the Haftarah of Yeshaya shows against Yechezkel's. He closes: never think like Amalek, never give up.

en: The theme of Parshas Yisro is hinted in its name: Yisro was a convert brought close, and the sedra tells those who are far to come near.
The nechshalim were expelled from under the Clouds of Glory, but Hashem did not reject them; their own lateness and lack of eagerness put them outside the camp.
Yisro felt he had come too late, and the two episodes he heard about, Kriyas Yam Suf and the war of Amalek, gave him the courage to come anyway.
Matan Torah is read twice a year: on Shavuos for those who prepared with sefirah, and in Parshas Yisro as a rerun for latecomers, so one is never too late.
Shavuos stands for an awakening from below that a person earns, while Parshas Yisro stands for an awakening from above that Hashem gives as a gift.
The Haftarah of Shavuos has Yechezkel pass through barriers in a place of purity, while the Haftarah of Yisro has Yeshaya see Hashem at once in a time of impurity.
The Rav says no one should let Amalek convince him that he does not belong; one should think like Yisro and, if needed, call someone out to pull him in.

candidateTopics: Shavuos and sefirah as preparation for Matan Torah
awakening from above and from below
Haftarah of Yisro and Haftarah of Shavuos

title.en: Va'avi eschem eilai and Ahavah Rabbah

summary.en: The Rav opens with Hashem's words before Matan Torah, 'I brought you to Me', which the Targum renders 'I brought you close to Me'. He explains that in the Ahavah Rabbah blessing we ask for understanding of Torah on the strength of this declared wish of Hashem.

title.en: The sedra's theme in Yisro's name

summary.en: The Rav says the theme of a sedra is hinted in its name: Yisro was a convert brought close, and the sedra beckons those who are far. He explains that Yisro asked Moshe to come out and greet him not for honor but because he feared he would lose courage before entering.

title.en: What Yisro heard: Yam Suf and Amalek

summary.en: The Rav asks why Rashi says Yisro heard specifically of Kriyas Yam Suf and the war of Amalek, when the passuk lists much more. He turns to the war of Amalek and Parshas Zachor, asking why the Torah stresses 'asher karcha baderech', on the road.

title.en: The nechshalim: latecomers or expelled?

summary.en: The Rav contrasts the Targum, which renders nechshalim as latecomers, with Rashi, who says they were members of Shevet Dan expelled from under the Clouds of Glory. He explains that the camp under the clouds had the holiness of Yerushalayim, so a metzora such as Miriam had to leave it.

title.en: They expelled themselves by being late

summary.en: The Rav reconciles the Targum and Rashi: when the trumpets signaled travel, the stragglers of Dan's camp took their time and fell behind, so their own attitude, not Hashem, expelled them. He compares one who skips a minyan or a shiur, and explains that Amalek could reach them only on the road.

title.en: Parshas Zachor: Hashem's care for the rejected

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem's anger at Amalek for attacking these estranged Jews has not cooled after thousands of years. Parshas Zachor is the one portion Hashem commands us to read from the Torah, more than Shema or the Ten Commandments, to impress on us how He cares for those who seem expelled.

title.en: Dasan and Aviram's private Kriyas Yam Suf

summary.en: The Rav brings the Targum Yonasan that Dasan and Aviram were the only Jews who stayed in Mitzrayim. According to the Midrash, when they saw the Egyptians drown they too wanted to go, and Hashem split the sea again just for these two latecomers.

title.en: Torah needs preparation; Yisro came after

summary.en: The Rav says Torah requires toil and preparation, which is why Hashem gave forty-nine days of counting before Matan Torah, and every year before Shavuos. Yisro missed all of it and wanted to break through the barrier of the Clouds of Glory, which no gentile could enter, as the sefarim say of a sukkah.

title.en: The latecomer's courage and the vav

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yisro first held back, feeling he was too late, but the stories of Dasan and Aviram and of Amalek showed him that Hashem welcomes latecomers. He came, added a parasha to the Torah, and received the vav, the letter of attachment shaped like a nail, in his name.

title.en: Two readings of Matan Torah

summary.en: The Rav explains that Matan Torah is read on Shavuos, starting directly from the third month, for those who prepared, and again in Parshas Yisro, introduced by the latecomer Yisro. The sefarim say the same light of Shavuos comes down on Parshas Yisro, so a person who missed his preparation learns that he is never too late.

title.en: Awakening from above and from below

summary.en: The Rav introduces the terms awakening from above and awakening from below. Shavuos is an awakening from below, winding one's own alarm clock; Parshas Yisro stands for an awakening from above, and only Hashem knows whom He awakens and for whom He waits.

title.en: Yechezkel's barriers, Yeshaya's direct vision

summary.en: The Rav compares the Haftarah of Shavuos, where Yechezkel passes four barriers before seeing the Throne of Glory, with the Haftarah of Yisro, where Yeshaya sees Hashem on His throne in the very first passuk. Parshas Yisro, he says, needs no preparation and no counting.

title.en: Purity by the river, impurity under Uziyahu

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yechezkel prophesied in Bavel by a river, a place of purity, while Yeshaya's vision came in the year Uziyahu became a metzora, when impurity rested on the nation through its king. Yeshaya himself felt unworthy, being of impure lips, yet the heavens opened for him.

title.en: A gift from heaven; Amalek's cold water

summary.en: The Rav says Parshas Yisro, framed by Yisro's story and this Haftarah, teaches that one may reach heights he did not earn. He brings the Midrash in which Hashem says He brings close and does not reject, and the Midrash that Amalek 'cooled off' the stragglers by telling them they did not belong.

title.en: Think like Yisro, not like Amalek

summary.en: The Rav concludes that one should not think like Amalek but like Yisro: if one cannot enter alone, he should call someone out to pull him in, and never give up. He returns to Ahavah Rabbah: we ask for Torah not as beggars at the door, since Hashem has declared that He wants us close.

title.en: Questions on Kedusha and Shemoneh Esrei

summary.en: In answer to questions, the Rav agrees that Kedusha is a kind of opening of the heavens, where we stand with the angels. He then discusses whether Shemoneh Esrei was instituted by the Avos or in place of the korbanos, and why its text, set with ruach hakodesh, must be kept.

catalogTitle: וכי ימוך אחיך - נפילה ממדריגתו - אחרי נמכר' גאולה תהיה לו!! (שייכות לשבועות)

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Shabbos, Eretz Yisrael, Yom Kippur, the Torah and the Jewish soul share one root, that a Jew's sins are only incidental to him, and that therefore no Jew, however far he falls, can be cut off from his root: after he is sold, redemption will come to him.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Rashi's comparison of shemittah to Shabbos Bereishis and shows that neither exists for rest; both are for Hashem's name. What appears in time also appears in place and in the soul: Shabbos among the days, Eretz Yisrael among the lands and the Jewish soul among the nations all stem from one root, together with the Torah. Eretz Yisrael is olam haba; its inner side is the Jewish soul, so it is not a mere object of a mitzvah, and the land itself keeps Shabbos. Yom Kippur and Yovel return every Jew to his root. Through the Maharal, the bris bein habesarim and Avraham's question, he explains that sin is only incidental to a Jew, like dirt on a diamond. The same answer resolves Yirmiyahu's question in the haftarah. Even a Jew sold to idolatry is redeemed, and the counting until Shavuos is the work of cleaning the diamond so that heaven comes down to each Jew.

en: Shemittah, like Shabbos Bereishis, is 'for Hashem' and not for rest, since the first Shabbos came right after creation, before anyone was tired.
Shabbos in time, Eretz Yisrael in place and the Jewish soul among the nations are parallel, and in their root they are one together with the Torah and Hashem.
Eretz Yisrael corresponds to olam haba, and its inner side is the Jewish soul, which tourists who see only its outside do not reach.
A sin is not the essence of a Jew but only incidental to him, like dirt on a diamond, and this is why korbanos, Yom Kippur and Yovel can wipe it away.
However low a Jew falls, even to being sold to idolatry itself, he cannot be torn from his root, and he will be redeemed.
The work of the days of sefirah until Shavuos is to clean away the dirt covering the diamond, so that heaven can come down to each Jew.

candidateTopics: sin as incidental to a Jew

title.en: Shemittah for Hashem, not for rest

summary.en: The Rav asks how shemittah can be for the land's rest when Rashi compares it to Shabbos Bereishis, which came before anyone needed rest. He then lays out that what exists in time exists in place and in the soul: Shabbos, Eretz Yisrael and the Jewish soul stand apart from the weekdays, other lands and the nations.

title.en: Eretz Yisrael is olam haba

summary.en: The Rav explains that Shabbos, Knesses Yisrael and Eretz Yisrael are united in their root: Shabbos is a taste of olam haba and Eretz Yisrael corresponds to olam haba, so every Jew who has a share in olam haba has a share in the land. He brings that the whole Torah is written across Eretz Yisrael, and explains through Osniel ben Kenaz and Kiryas Sefer how forgotten halachos were tied to a place in the land.

title.en: The inner Yerushalayim and the outer

summary.en: The Rav calls Shabbos the source of Jewish souls and Yom Kippur the root of that root, then brings the Gemara's distinction between the Yerushalayim of this world, which anyone may go up to, and that of olam haba. Tourists see only the outside of the land, just as the inner light of many Jews is hidden, and he compares this to Jews who watch the clock on Shabbos and those who cannot part from it.

title.en: The land itself keeps Shabbos

summary.en: The Rav explains that because the inner side of Eretz Yisrael is the Jewish soul, the Torah does not treat the land like tzitzis, an object used for a mitzvah; rather the land itself keeps the mitzvah, and its mitzvah is Shabbos. Just as Jews need Eretz Yisrael, the land needs Jews, which is why the tochachah ends with the remembrance of the land, and each Jew has his own portion in it, as he has his own letter in the Sefer Torah.

title.en: Yom Kippur and Yovel return to the root

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yom Kippur, the root of Jewish souls, is the day of returning to the root, which only Jews have, and that even Jews far from Yiddishkeit feel connected to it. Yovel begins on Yom Kippur, when every Jew returns to his ancestral portion, the fiftieth gate.

title.en: Why the Torah was forced on Yisrael

summary.en: The Rav brings the Maharal's question why Hashem had to force the Torah on Yisrael after they said na'aseh v'nishma, and his answer that the Torah must come by necessity, since a level reached by choice can be lost while what is necessary is eternal. He adds the Midrash comparing Yisrael to a woman taken by force, who may never be sent away, and turns to the bris bein habesarim, where Klal Yisrael was born.

title.en: Sin is only incidental to a Jew

summary.en: The Rav explains Avraham's question 'bameh eida' as the fear that sin would uproot his children from the land, and Hashem's answer, korbanos, as the revelation that sin is incidental to a Jew and not his essence, unlike the nations. He illustrates with ink poured into water versus dirt on a person or a diamond, brings the Midrash on Yaakov as 'ish chalak', and shows that Yom Kippur and Yovel reveal the same truth.

title.en: Sold even to idolatry, still redeemed

summary.en: The Rav reads 'ki yamuch achicha' as the step-by-step fall of a Jew, down to being sold to 'eker mishpachas ger', which Rashi explains as idolatry itself. Precisely there the Torah calls idolatry 'eker', destined to be uprooted, because a Jew's root can never be torn away and sin is only incidental to him.

title.en: Yirmiyahu buys a field

summary.en: The Rav goes through the haftarah: as Yerushalayim is besieged, Hashem tells Yirmiyahu to buy his cousin Chanamel's field as a sign that fields will again be bought in the land. Yirmiyahu asks how this fits, and the Rav explains that his question is Avraham's: if sin causes exile and teshuvah brings return, why promise the return now, in the midst of the sins.

title.en: Hashem's answer and the redeeming relative

summary.en: The Rav explains Hashem's answer to Yirmiyahu: sin is only incidental to Jews, and Hashem will gather them, give them one heart and plant them in the land. He reads the redemption by a relative as redemption through a tzaddik of the same soul-root, and concludes that in Yovel the root is revealed: every Jewish soul is bound into Yom Kippur, Shabbos, Eretz Yisrael and the Torah.

title.en: Shavuos, the fiftieth day, and heaven coming down

summary.en: The Rav compares Shavuos and Yom Kippur, the giving of the first and the last luchos, both the fiftieth gate; the luchos broke only on the outside. The counting is the work of cleaning the diamond so that heaven reaches each Jew, who is himself a Har Sinai. He closes that the Torah was given in the desert to show that when Jews cannot reach their root, the root comes to them.

catalogTitle: שמיטה ויובל - להיות מובדל מגשמיות וזה מביא השתוקקות לה' (שבועות)

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that everything yearns for its root, that gashmiyus blocks that yearning, and that Shabbos, Shemitah and Yovel free a Jew from it so that he returns to Hashem and is ready for the Torah of Shavuos.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Midrash that when Hashem came to give the Torah the sea fled and the mountains danced, but the desert rejoiced. Everything is drawn to its root, he explains, and gashmiyus is a barrier like clay between a magnet and iron; the bare desert had no barrier, so the Torah was given there. Parshas Behar's Shemitah is the land's Shabbos: the world was made for toil, and Shabbos returns a person to his root by showing that Hashem, not man, provides. Yovel, the fiftieth year, rises higher still, above nature and mazal, and every Jew returns to his portion of Eretz Yisrael, whose inner side is the Torah. From the Jew's yearning for Eretz Yisrael and the bond of husband and wife, the Rav moves to Yom Kippur, Shavuos and Shabbos as a return to the Mikdash, and to the greater longing of galus. He closes with preparing for Shavuos.

en: Everything has a natural pull toward its root, and gashmiyus is the barrier that stops a Jew from feeling his pull toward Hashem.
The Torah was given in the desert because a place empty of gashmiyus has no barrier, and so too a person who makes himself like a desert merits Torah.
Shabbos and Shemitah return a person to his root by showing that Hashem gives everything and man produces nothing.
Yovel, the fiftieth year, stands above nature and mazal; in it every Jew returns to his portion of Eretz Yisrael, whose inner side is the Torah.
A Jew can only grow from Eretz Yisrael, the place from which Adam HaRishon was formed, which is why Jews have yearned for it through two thousand years of galus.
In galus a Jew can feel a greater longing for Hashem, and a greater taste of Shabbos, than in the time of the Beis HaMikdash.

husband and wife as one soul

title.en: Places with mazal; the desert that rejoiced

summary.en: The Rav notes that certain places, like certain times, are suited to a person, as in the Gemara's 'changing place changes mazal'. He then brings a Midrash: when Hashem came to give the Torah, the sea fled and the mountains danced, but the desert received Him with joy.

title.en: Everything yearns for its root

summary.en: The Rav explains that everything is drawn to its source, and since all comes from Hashem all should be drawn to Him; gashmiyus blocks this like clay between a magnet and iron. The desert, empty of gashmiyus, had no barrier, so the Torah, which asked for its portion among the poor, was given there; one who makes himself like a desert merits Torah, and a Jew who does not feel drawn to Hashem is blocked by gashmiyus.

title.en: Shemitah as the land's Shabbos

summary.en: Turning to Parshas Behar, the Rav asks what connection Shabbos has with a piece of land, and answers that Eretz Yisrael has an inner side bound to the Torah. He explains that the world was made for toil, which distances a person from Hashem, so Hashem gave Shabbos, meaning both stopping and returning, to bring him back to his root.

title.en: Why man works, and how Shabbos returns him

summary.en: The Rav explains that man does not truly produce his livelihood; Hashem wants him to work only because Adam's sin scattered holy sparks that must be gathered back. Shabbos brings him back to Gan Eden, and by resting he testifies that Hashem provides everything, which is the same lesson as Shemitah.

title.en: Shemitas kesafim and the test of Shemitah

summary.en: The Rav explains why the release of debts depends on the release of land: in the Shemitah year a farmer has no crop and needs cash to buy food, yet the Torah tells him to let his debts go. Those who keep Shemitah are the 'mighty in strength', and through it a person reaches the true Shabbos and bonds with Hashem.

title.en: Yovel: above nature, back to the field

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yovel, two rest years in a row, brings a Jew to the root of emunah that Avraham received when Hashem raised him above mazal and nature. In Yovel every Jew returns to his own field, an empty field like the desert, and the Rav brings the Gemara of Osniel ben Kenaz and the 3,000 forgotten halachos to show that each part of Eretz Yisrael corresponds to a part of the Torah.

title.en: Adam from the place of the mizbeach

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem and the Jewish people yearn for each other, though barriers can hide it. All Jewish souls were part of Adam HaRishon, who was formed from the earth of the mizbeach in Eretz Yisrael like a plant from its soil; therefore a Jew can only grow from Eretz Yisrael, which is why earth from there is placed in graves abroad.

title.en: Mesirus nefesh for one's root

summary.en: The Rav explains that every being gives itself for its root: nations die for their fatherland, and Jews have yearned for Eretz Yisrael for two thousand years. He brings the Zohar that Eretz Yisrael is bound to bris milah, so Yishmael's descendants hold it until Jews return, but their tie is only to its outer shell, not its inner side.

title.en: Husband and wife, and the mizbeach's tears

summary.en: The Rav explains that Adam and Chava were created as one and cut apart, so husband and wife yearn for each other more than a child for his parents. This explains the Gemara that the mizbeach weeps over one who divorces his first wife, since their souls were one at the place of the mizbeach; the Sotah's water with earth from the Mishkan's floor testifies to the same bond.

title.en: The fiftieth: Yom Kippur, Shavuos and the shofar

summary.en: The Rav explains that in Yovel every Jew returns to his root, Hashem and the Torah, as on the fiftieth day of Shavuos. Yom Kippur lifts a Jew up to heaven, while Shavuos brings heaven down so that even chametz becomes a vessel for holiness. The shofar of Yovel's Yom Kippur reveals the beauty at the root of everything, and 'yovel' itself means a stream, a source.

title.en: The place of the Mikdash came to Sinai

summary.en: The Rav says that reading Parshas Behar is a preparation for Shavuos, when one is freed of the barriers that hold back the yearning for Hashem, like the desert and not the sea and mountains. He explains that the place of the Mikdash came to Har Sinai in the desert, bringing the Ohr HaChaim that it traveled with the Jews, which also answers a hard Gemara about the Mishkan; every Shabbos returns a Jew to that place.

title.en: Shabbos as the Mikdash; the longing of galus

summary.en: Bringing Rav Tzadok HaKohen that the main counting of the Omer is on Shabbos, the Rav explains that Shabbos and the Torah are the Beis HaMikdash of today. In galus a Jew who prepares for Shabbos can have a greater Mikdash and a greater thirst for Hashem than in the time of the Mikdash. He brings the Bnei Yissaschar that Eretz Yisrael is ruled by din while galus is ruled by rachamim, like a father with a sick child.

title.en: Women first at Sinai; preparing for Shavuos

summary.en: The Rav explains the Midrash that at Sinai the women were addressed first: at creation Adam was commanded before Chava by rank, but the Torah was given as a complete union beyond rank and reckoning. He closes by saying that this Shabbos, when Yovel is read, is the main preparation for Shavuos, and that the mikveh and Shavuos itself, like Yom Kippur, belong to the fiftieth gate.

catalogTitle: ארבעה דברים ששכח משה כי הם בחינת יובל

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the four laws Moshe Rabbeinu had to ask about (the blasphemer, the wood-gatherer, Pesach Sheni and the daughters of Tzelofchad) all belong to the hidden realm of Yovel, which is beyond intellectual grasp, and draws from this the holiness of every Jew.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael whether the details of the Torah were given at Sinai, and asks why, according to Targum Yonasan, there were four laws Moshe did not know. Rashi's question why shemitah is tied to Har Sinai leads him to Yovel: the Ramban says the fiftieth gate, which is Yovel, was not revealed to Moshe. Yovel corresponds to the first two letters of Hashem's Name, the hidden 'Atika' beyond grasp, where every Jew returns to his root. Each of the four laws touches Yovel. The daughters of Tzelofchad grasped with feeling what cold intellect cannot; the wood-gatherer was liable by law yet acted for Heaven; and the blasphemer, son of Shlomis bas Divri, mocked the nine-day-old showbread because he denied the holiness of the Jewish camp. The Rav ends with the tochachah, the days of Sefirah and preparing for Shavuos.

en: The four laws Moshe had to ask about were given at Sinai, but they were hidden from him because they belong to Yovel, which is above his grasp.
Yovel is the fiftieth gate and corresponds to the first two letters of Hashem's Name, the hidden 'Atika', where every Jew and all of creation return to their root.

Matters of Yovel are grasped through feeling, symbolized by wine, rather than through the cold logical intellect symbolized by bread; this is why the daughters of Tzelofchad sensed what Moshe did not.
The showbread represents the holiness of Klal Yisrael, and its staying fresh shows that the Jewish camp is never 'stale'; the blasphemer denied this.
Everything, including the matters beyond grasp, was given at Sinai, since the revealed Torah holds the hidden within it; this is why shemitah is tied to Har Sinai.
The days of Sefirah, especially the last two weeks, are a time to turn the forty-nine curses of the tochachah and the bad middos into blessings and return to the root.

candidateTopics: four laws moshe did not know

title.en: Four laws Moshe did not know

summary.en: The Rav presents the dispute of Rabbi Akiva and Rabbi Yishmael whether the details of the Torah were given at Sinai, and the Targum Yonasan's list of four laws Moshe did not know. He asks why, if all was given at Sinai, Moshe had to ask about them.

title.en: Shemitah, Sinai and the blasphemer's exit

summary.en: The Rav brings Rashi's question why shemitah is mentioned with Har Sinai, and the Zohar that 'yesh' stands for Yovel and Shemitah. He turns to the blasphemer at the end of Emor, the first of the four laws, and to Rashi's 'from his world he went out', asking what it means.

title.en: Mocking the nine-day-old showbread

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that the blasphemer came out of the parsha of the showbread and mocked a king eating nine-day-old bread. He asks how a man of about seventy, who had seen the Exodus, the splitting of the sea and Sinai, could fall to such mockery.

title.en: The camp as a living Sefer Torah

summary.en: The Rav asks why the blasphemer was not allowed to camp in the tribe of Dan, and explains that the Jewish camp was arranged like the camps of angels around the Throne, a living Sefer Torah of 600,000 letters that a stranger would invalidate. He then adds that the mockery hid a denial of the miracle that the showbread stayed fresh.

title.en: Yovel, the fiftieth gate and the root

summary.en: The Rav explains shemitah as the Shabbos of the land and Yovel as the fiftieth gate the Ramban says Moshe did not attain. Yovel corresponds to the first two letters of Hashem's Name, called Atika, beyond any grasp; on Shabbos one returns partly to the root, and at Yovel everyone returns to his root, as on Shavuos, the uncounted fiftieth day.

title.en: The large nun of the daughters of Tzelofchad

summary.en: The Rav states that all four laws relate to Yovel, which is why Moshe had to ask. He brings Rabbeinu Bachya that the large nun in 'mishpatan' alludes to the fiftieth gate, and asks why the daughters of Tzelofchad knew what Moshe did not.

title.en: Wine and feeling, bread and intellect

summary.en: The Rav brings the Maharal that the matzos correspond to the Avos and the cups of wine to the Imahos, and explains that wine is feeling and intuition while grain is intellect. Women grasp with feeling, but a ruling must come from cold intellect, and he tells of a posek who would not rule after a woman's tears stirred him.

title.en: A portion in the land, a portion in Torah

summary.en: The Rav explains that a portion in Eretz Yisrael corresponds to a letter of the Torah and to one's root, which returns at Yovel. The daughters of Tzelofchad felt that no Jew can be cast off, as the wise woman told Dovid; Moshe's cold intellect could not reach it because it belongs to Yovel.

title.en: The wood-gatherer and Pesach Sheni

summary.en: The Rav explains that the wood-gatherer acted for the sake of Heaven to teach that Shabbos still binds; by law he was liable, but in the depth known only to Hashem he was not, which is a matter of Yovel. Pesach Sheni likewise connects a Jew to his root, and those who asked 'lamah nigara' were right in feeling.

title.en: The showbread and the holiness of Yisrael

summary.en: Coming to the fourth law, the Rav explains that the showbread alludes to the holiness of Yisrael: twelve loaves against the twelve tribes and the angels above, arranged six and six for yesod, and staying fresh because true holiness never decays. Hashem testifies with the letters yud and hei on every Jewish family, and the only blemish was Shlomis bas Divri.

title.en: Shlomis and Shulamis

summary.en: The Rav brings Rashi that Shlomis greeted everyone and chattered with all, and the Chasam Sofer's question why Knesses Yisrael is called Shulamis. He explains that Shulamis is a passive form: Klal Yisrael receives greetings from the nations but does not mingle with them, while Shlomis' greeting everyone cost her son his place in the camp.

title.en: The showbread and kiddush of Shabbos day

summary.en: The Rav says the showbread too is beyond grasp. The Shabbos day meal belongs to Atika and Yovel, which is why kiddush then is on wine and done standing, and why the Arizal's song for that meal mentions the twelve loaves.

title.en: The blasphemer's claim against the camp

summary.en: The Rav returns to 'from his world he went out': from the 'chok olam' of the showbread, the world of Yovel. The blasphemer, lacking a root there, claimed the showbread was stale like a Jewish camp of mixed lineage; Hashem commanded the bread kept nine days to teach that all Jews are holy and must be loved.

title.en: Torah from Sinai: revealed and hidden

summary.en: The Rav brings the Maharal on 'Moshe kibel Torah miSinai', that Sinai shows the Torah came down into this world, and asks whether the Yovel matters were then not given at Sinai. He answers with the Zohar that the four letters of Hashem's Name are bound together: the revealed Torah holds the hidden within it, so Moshe received everything at Sinai, though what is above grasp could later be hidden from him.

title.en: Why shemitah stands by Har Sinai

summary.en: The Rav answers Rashi's opening question: shemitah, the whole parsha of Yovel, is tied to Har Sinai to teach that even its details, though bound to Yovel, were given at Sinai. That is why the parsha of Behar follows right after the blasphemer, the first of the four laws.

title.en: Turning the curses into blessings

summary.en: The Rav links the forty-nine curses of the tochachah to the forty-nine bad middos that must be transformed during Sefirah through holiness. He tells of the Ba'al HaTanya's son who fainted on hearing the tochachah, having heard only blessings from his father, and of Reb Hershele Zidichoiver crying out at the tochachah.

title.en: Sefirah, Shavuos and returning to the root

summary.en: The Rav describes the days of Sefirah as holy days like chol hamoed, the parsha ending with Yovel and 'b'Har Sinai', and Megillas Rus as a return to the root. He closes asking that everyone prepare for Shavuos with good middos, Torah and tefillah, and merit the fiftieth day.

catalogTitle: A Time to reaffirm our Acceptance of the תורה

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Shabbos Yisro is a renewed Matan Torah for those who came late, and that one who truly gives himself over to Torah stands, like the Kodesh HaKodashim, above all calculation.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Rashi's question of what Yisro heard, and says every Shabbos is unique, so that Shabbos Yisro is a rerun of the acceptance of the Torah, driven by Shabbos itself. Yisro lacked the preparation of the Exodus, Sefirah and the war with Amalek; what gave him courage? The Rav brings the Midrash that Dasan and Aviram, who stayed in Egypt, came late to the sea and Hashem split it again for them, and Rashi's account of the Bnei Dan, left outside the clouds of glory and attacked by Amalek, for whom Hashem still wages war. Hearing that Hashem does not reject latecomers, Yisro came. The Rav then reads the Rambam that any person who devotes himself to Torah becomes like shevet Levi. He asks why the Masorah counts 72 pesukim in Yisro when he counted 75, rejects one answer, and concludes that, like the Aron in the Kodesh HaKodashim, Torah is beyond arithmetic; so too the sincere ben Torah's parnassah, though this is not for everyone.

en: Every Shabbos is unique, and Shabbos Yisro is a renewal of the acceptance of the Torah, read because of the Shabbos itself.
Yisro lacked the preparation the rest of Klal Yisrael had for Matan Torah, and his courage came from hearing that Hashem does not reject those who come late.
Dasan and Aviram, who came late to the sea, and the Bnei Dan, who fell behind the clouds of glory, are two cases where Hashem stood by latecomers because they are His children.
Parshas Yisro is a second chance at Matan Torah for those who were not ready on Shavuos.
Just as the Aron in the Kodesh HaKodashim took up no space, Torah is not bound by arithmetic, which answers why the Masorah counts 72 pesukim where the Rav counted 75.
According to the Rambam, anyone who sincerely devotes himself to Torah becomes holy of holies and is provided for, but the Rav stresses this is only for genuine, G-d-fearing people.

Amalek and the stragglers of Dan
Rambam on shevet Levi and devotion to Torah

title.en: Each parsha and each Shabbos is unique

summary.en: The Rav opens with Rashi's question of what Yisro heard, then says the parsha is a cloth woven of its pesukim in which everything that happens can be found, that parshiyos may not be mixed, and, citing the Lechovitcher, that every Shabbos is unique and each Jew has his own Shabbos.

title.en: Shabbos Yisro and Yisro's missing preparation

summary.en: The Rav says Shabbos Yisro is a rerun of the acceptance of the Torah, perhaps stronger than Shavuos, then asks how Yisro could come to accept the Torah without the Exodus, Sefirah and the war against Amalek that prepared everyone else.

title.en: The sea split again for Dasan and Aviram

summary.en: On the passuk that Pharaoh would say of the Jews that they are confused, the Rav brings Rashi and the Targum that Dasan and Aviram stayed in Egypt, and a Midrash cited by the Be'er Mayim Chaim that they came late and Hashem split the sea for them alone, which explains why Tehillim says Hashem rebuked the sea.

title.en: Amalek and the Bnei Dan left behind

summary.en: On the passuk that Amalek struck the stragglers, the Rav explains with Rashi that some of the tribe of Dan fell outside the clouds of glory and were attacked, that Hashem never evicts a child, and that His war against Amalek still burns because Amalek attacked His children who were late.

title.en: Never too late: Matan Torah again

summary.en: The Rav concludes that these two stories gave Yisro the courage to come though late, and that Parshas Yisro is Matan Torah for those not ready on Shavuos; he then begins the Rambam at the end of Hilchos Shemitah v'Yovel about shevet Levi.

title.en: Not only shevet Levi: the Rambam

summary.en: After noting how many seforim and roshei yeshiva come from Kohanim and Leviim, the Rav reads the Rambam that not only shevet Levi but any person whose spirit moves him to stand before Hashem is sanctified and provided for, and brings Dovid HaMelech's passuk as proof.

title.en: The Masorah's 72 pesukim and the count of 75

summary.en: The Rav notes that the Masorah at the end of Yisro gives 72 pesukim with the sign Yanadav, yet he counted 75; he suggests the Aseres HaDibros are counted by the ta'am elyon as ten dibros, then rejects it, since a pasuk or an aliyah cannot be that short.

title.en: Above arithmetic like the Kodesh HaKodashim

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that the place of the Aron took up no space, and says that in the realm of Torah arithmetic does not apply, so 72 against 75 is no question, just as the Torah given on the fifty-first day counts as fifty; he adds the Bnei Yissaschar's demonstration that people spend more than they earn.

title.en: Yanadav: the volunteer above calculation

summary.en: Returning to the Rambam, the Rav links the sign Yanadav to the one whose spirit volunteers and who casts off the yoke of calculations, becoming holy of holies with his parnassah assured; he warns, with the dispute of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Rabbi Yishmael and the Ba'al Shem Tov, that this is only for the sincere, not for those following peer pressure.

catalogTitle: ארץ ישראל שהוא "יהודי" שבארצות - שבתה שבת לה'

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Eretz Yisrael is the 'Jew' among lands and the Shabbos of the world, so it keeps shemitah and yovel, and that yovel, like Shavuos, returns every Jew to his root in the Torah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the Chasam Sofer, who says that in the yovel year people will not need to eat, like at Matan Torah, and asks how this fits the blessings of Bechukosai, which speak of eating. He then asks why the land must 'rest' at all. Everything has a body and a soul: as there is a separation between a Jew and a gentile, so there is between Shabbos and weekdays, and between Eretz Yisrael and other lands. Eretz Yisrael is the Shabbos of the world; shemitah is its Shabbos, and yovel is its Yom Kippur and Shavuos, a level above the world, where there is no eating. Eretz Yisrael below corresponds to Eretz Yisrael above, olam haba, and is a Sefer Torah whose every place holds a halachah; every Jew is a letter. Yovel, Shavuos and the redemption return each Jew to his root, as with Rus and Osniel ben Kenaz. He closes with bitachon, preparation in the sefirah days, the segulos of Sefer Chareidim, and honoring Shabbos.

en: As there is a separation between a Jew and a gentile, there is the same separation between Shabbos and the weekdays and between Eretz Yisrael and other lands.
Eretz Yisrael is the Shabbos of the world, and because a land's time moves slowly, its Shabbos comes every seventh year: shemitah.
Yovel is the higher Shabbos, parallel to Yom Kippur and Shavuos, a level above the world where there is no eating.
Eretz Yisrael below corresponds to Eretz Yisrael above, which is olam haba, and every Jew is planted there.
Eretz Yisrael is a Sefer Torah: every place in it holds a halachah, and every Jew is a letter with his own place in it.
Yovel, Shavuos and the final redemption return every Jew to his root and his letter in the Torah.

Eretz Yisrael above and olam haba
Eretz Yisrael as a Sefer Torah
every Jew a letter in the Torah

title.en: The Chasam Sofer: no eating in yovel

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara about Pinchas ben Yair's donkey and the Chasam Sofer, who says that in yovel people will not eat, as at Matan Torah, so only animals will eat the produce. He asks how this fits the blessings of Bechukosai, which speak of eating, both in the days of Moshiach and in the world of souls.

title.en: Why the land must rest: Jew, Shabbos and Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Rav asks why the parsha opens with the land's Shabbos before the six years of work, and how a field can rest. He answers that everything has a body and a soul: the separation between a Jew and a gentile also exists between Shabbos and weekdays and between Eretz Yisrael and other lands, a different reality that only clear eyes see.

title.en: Shemitah as Shabbos, yovel as Yom Kippur and Shavuos

summary.en: Eretz Yisrael is the Shabbos of the world, and since a land's time is slow, its Shabbos is every seventh year. Yovel is the higher Shabbos, like Yom Kippur and Shavuos, the fiftieth level above counting and above the world; it is proclaimed on Yom Kippur as freedom, and Shavuos is the freedom of the Torah.

title.en: Answering the question: eating as avodah, yovel as Yom Kippur

summary.en: The Rav answers his opening question: in the days of Moshiach people will eat, because eating is an avodah of refinement that angels cannot do. But yovel is like Yom Kippur, a day above this world, so in yovel there is no eating, as Moshe did not eat on Sinai; the produce is eaten only by the animals.

title.en: Eretz Yisrael above and olam haba

summary.en: Turning to Pirkei Avos in the sefirah days, the Rav asks how 'all Israel have a share in olam haba' is proven from the verse about inheriting the land. Eretz Yisrael below corresponds to Eretz Yisrael above, which is olam haba, where Hashem planted every Jewish soul; even a Jew cut off for a time will return.

title.en: Eretz Yisrael as a Sefer Torah

summary.en: Walking four amos in Eretz Yisrael assures olam haba, since the land below mirrors the land above. Through Osniel ben Kenaz, who restored forgotten halachos when he won Kiryas Sefer, the Rav shows that every place in Eretz Yisrael holds a halachah, that the land is a Sefer Torah, and that every Jew is one of its letters.

title.en: Yovel and Shavuos return each Jew to his root

summary.en: A Jew who leaves Eretz Yisrael is cut off from his root, yet through Torah he stays connected. In yovel, the light of the fifty gates, every man returns to his holding; in time this is Shavuos, the fiftieth day, when each Jew is 'recharged'. The Tikkun of Shavuos night goes through all of Torah so that each finds his letter, and the Aseres Hadibros contain all of Torah.

title.en: Letters join into a Torah: unity and learning

summary.en: The parshiyos before Shavuos prepare for it: Behar speaks of shemitah and yovel, rising step by step. A single letter cannot be read; only joined into words, verses and parshiyos does it reveal Hashem's will, so all Jews must be united, 'and great shall be the peace of your children'. The Rishonim say the purpose of shemitah and yovel is to sit and learn.

title.en: Megillas Rus: returning on Shavuos

summary.en: On Shavuos we read Rus: Elimelech's family left for Moav and was cut off, and Naomi returns together with Rus, from whom comes David. Boaz renews the halachah of 'a Moabite, not a Moabitess' together with a field, just as Osniel did. Yovel applies only when all Jews dwell in the land, since yovel means return.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a soul of yovel

summary.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is a soul of yovel, so the halachah follows him in the laws of Shabbos. In the dispute in Berachos about working the field or only learning, the halachah now does not follow him, but in yovel and the redemption it will. Each Jew is a letter in a family of letters, and peace makes the Sefer Torah whole; keeping shemitah needs great bitachon.

title.en: Bitachon and the thief who cut himself off

summary.en: The Rav brings the Rambam about those devoted like the tribe of Levi and the haftarah 'Blessed is the man who trusts in Hashem'. The thief lacked bitachon: his food was decreed anyway, and by stealing he cut himself off from his letter in the Torah, so he is sold to eat from a root not his own, until yovel returns him. He ends with the hope for the great shofar.

title.en: Preparing in the sefirah days

summary.en: The sefirah weeks prepare for Shavuos: each week is a kind of shemitah, but some Jews are so attached to exile that only yovel brings them out. The Rav calls for teshuvah, toil in Torah, tefillah and refining middos, cites the Sfas Emes on learning all Shavuos night, and introduces the last page of Sefer Chareidim on inexpensive remedies for the soul.

title.en: The segulos of Sefer Chareidim

summary.en: The Rav goes through the segulos of Sefer Chareidim: answering amen yehei shmei rabbah with all one's strength, which he explains as concentration rather than loudness; saying the Shirah daily with joy; overlooking slights; hisbodedus, where the Ba'al Shem Tov stressed being together with Jews; and listening eagerly to words of the wise.

title.en: Shabbos: halachos, clothing and minhagim

summary.en: Returning to the segulah of Shabbos, the Rav stresses learning hilchos Shabbos, special Shabbos clothing, and keeping the Jewish minhagim of Shabbos, with a story about a guest and the order of the Shabbos meal. He adds that one must rejoice in Shabbos, Hashem's hidden treasure, and receive Him as a guest.

title.en: Holy speech on Shabbos, toward Shavuos

summary.en: Shabbos is not a time for idle talk: the Rav brings the Midrash of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's mother, notes that Hashem created the world with sayings and rested from them, and cites the Shelah on delighting in Shabbos. He concludes that to prepare for Shavuos, the great Shabbos, one should take on Shabbos as a segulah.

catalogTitle: השייכות בין יובל ושמיטה לספירה ושבועות - בחינת חמישים

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that shemitah and yovel mirror the count of Sefirah and Shavuos: shemitah is the Shabbos and the Yerushalayim of time, while yovel, the fiftieth, is the Kodesh HaKodashim beyond time and place, the level of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and of the giving of the Torah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Rashi's question of what shemitah has to do with Sinai and answers that shemitah and yovel show that the whole Torah comes from Sinai: their seven sevens and the fiftieth year match Sefirah and Shavuos, the day of freedom engraved on the Luchos. He builds a parallel: what Shabbos is in time, Yerushalayim is in place. Yerushalayim is ownerless, undivided among the tribes, a home of kohanim, Torah and the poor; in shemitah all of Eretz Yisrael becomes Yerushalayim and every Jew a kohen. Yovel is higher still: the Beis HaMikdash and the Kodesh HaKodashim, beyond time and place, like Yom Kippur and the fiftieth day that is not counted. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the Shabbos of the soul and the yovel among people, which explains Lag BaOmer in Sefirah. He closes with the week of Hod, when the gates of the fiftieth are open and one need only listen.

en: Shemitah and yovel were chosen to teach that all of Torah is from Sinai, because their count of seven sevens and the fiftieth is the same as Sefirah and Shavuos.
Shabbos is the 'sukkah of peace' in time and Yerushalayim is the same in place: a private domain of Hashem set apart inside the world.
In shemitah the land becomes ownerless and Yerushalayim spreads over all of Eretz Yisrael, reminding a person that the land is Hashem's.
In shemitah every Jew becomes like a kohen, who has no portion of land and whose portion is Hashem.
Yovel is higher than shemitah: it is the Beis HaMikdash and the Kodesh HaKodashim, above time and place, and it is not counted in the cycle of years.
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai is the Shabbos and the yovel of the soul, which is why his day falls in Sefirah when the light of Shavuos begins.
In the week of Hod the gates of the fiftieth are open and announced, and the Rav urges listeners to listen and use these days.

the kohen and the twelve tribes
Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Lag BaOmer
Kodesh HaKodashim above time and place
holiness of Yerushalayim after the destruction

title.en: Shemitah, Sinai and the count to fifty

summary.en: After noting that the gates of heaven are open in these weeks, the Rav brings Rashi's question of what shemitah has to do with Sinai. He shows that the six years and shemitah, the seven cycles and yovel are the same as the seven weeks of Sefirah and Shavuos, and that yovel, like Shavuos, is the time of freedom engraved on the Luchos.

title.en: Shemitah and yovel as Torah from Sinai

summary.en: The Rav explains that shemitah, like Shabbos, frees Jews to learn, and yovel stands for a higher level of Torah. He compares the camp around Har Sinai and the Mishkan in the middle, and the Kohen Gadol entering the Kodesh HaKodashim on Yom Kippur of yovel to Moshe ascending the mountain, concluding that all Torah comes from the fifty gates.

title.en: Shabbos in time, Yerushalayim in place

summary.en: Hashem created everything in place, time and soul; Shabbos is the sukkas shalom in time and Yerushalayim, the sukkah Hashem made in the world, is the same in place. The Rav uses the laws of sukkah walls and of reshus hayachid to explain that both are Hashem's private domain set apart from this world.

title.en: Shemitah spreads Yerushalayim over the land

summary.en: In shemitah Yerushalayim, where nothing may be planted, spreads over all of Eretz Yisrael, as Shabbos will spread over all time in the future. The sixth year gives a double blessing like the manna of Friday. Shabbos and shemitah remind the farmer that Hashem, not he, is the owner; 'for the land is Mine', so the fields become ownerless.

title.en: Yerushalayim, an endless shemitah

summary.en: Yerushalayim was not divided among the tribes and its houses were not rented, so it is a constant shemitah. Shemitah is for the poor, unlike the communist imitation that brought slavery. Yerushalayim too is arranged for the poor through maaser sheni and korbanos, and it is the place of Torah: Hakhel in the shemitah year, the teachers of children and the Sanhedrin.

title.en: Kohanim, the tribes and Yaakov Avinu

summary.en: Yerushalayim is the place of the kohanim and levi'im, who have no portion; in shemitah every Jew becomes a kohen. The twelve tribes, like Rosh Chodesh and the twelve weekday blessings of Shemoneh Esrei, are a weekday concept, while Yaakov Avinu, the trunk above the branches, is Shabbos and belongs with Yerushalayim.

title.en: Eating 'yashan' and the step to yovel

summary.en: The Torah promises that in shemitah one eats 'yashan', which the Targum renders 'atika', recalling the Shabbos meals of Atika Kadisha and the Old City; in shemitah the whole land eats from Hashem's table as a foretaste of the future. The Rav then says yovel is higher still, the Beis HaMikdash, where the tribes who go up to Yerushalayim are elevated.

title.en: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, the Shabbos of the soul

summary.en: The Rav asks what Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai has to do with Sefirah and Shavuos. As Shabbos is in time and Yerushalayim in place, the kohen, and anyone who devotes himself to Torah as the Rambam writes, is so in the soul. Rabbi Shimon was called Shabbos; he held that one should learn Torah constantly, as the Gemara relates after the cave, and he is the 'Shabbos of Shabbosos', the fiftieth.

title.en: Yom Kippur, yovel and the Kodesh HaKodashim

summary.en: The shofar of yovel on Yom Kippur frees every slave and returns every man to his portion; it reveals a level above place and time, the fifty gates of binah, also drawn down at Sinai. The Kodesh HaKodashim is likewise above place: the Aron took no space, and this is not counted among the miracles because there it is natural.

title.en: The uncounted fiftieth and Lag BaOmer

summary.en: Yovel is not counted as part of the next cycle of years, and the fiftieth day of the omer is not counted either, because it is above time. Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's soul comes from this 'secret of fifty'; therefore on Lag BaOmer, when two thirds of Sefirah have passed, the light of Shavuos begins.

title.en: Emor and the lasting holiness of Yerushalayim

summary.en: Lag BaOmer usually falls in the week of Emor, which speaks of the kohanim and the Kohen Gadol, the level of Rabbi Shimon. The Rav brings the Rambam that the holiness of Eretz Yisrael from conquest was annulled, while Yerushalayim and the Mikdash keep their holiness, because they are holy through the Shechinah, which no conquest removes.

title.en: Fixed holiness, Rosh Chodesh and the kingdom of kohanim

summary.en: Rosh Chodesh, like the tribes and Eretz Yisrael, needs sanctification by beis din, while Shabbos and Yerushalayim are fixed by Hashem. The Rav ties Emor and Behar together with the Rambam's line that any Jew can become holy, and explains that on Shavuos every Jew enters the fiftieth, as the Baal HaTurim reads 'a kingdom of kohanim' as kohanim gedolim.

title.en: The week of Hod: the open gates

summary.en: The Rav adds that the level of yovel comes several times a year, as at the Exodus, when Jews entered the fifty gates. In the thirty days from Pesach the gates are open, but in the week of Hod it is announced; with the Baal Shem Tov's teaching about the daily heavenly voice, he urges listening, and closes with wishes for Lag BaOmer, Rosh Chodesh Sivan and Shavuos.

catalogTitle: תיקון לישראל הנמכר לעקר משפחת גר הוא ע"י יובל

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains yovel as every Jew's return to his root, and shows how even a Jew sold to 'the root of a stranger's family', to avodah zarah itself, is redeemed by yovel, through the secret hidden in every Jewish soul.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with yovel, the fiftieth year, as a return to the root, like Shavuos, the fiftieth day, and Olam Haba, from which every soul comes. Yovel is announced with the shofar of freedom, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, whose day is Lag BaOmer, is a soul of yovel: joy without churban, a Rebbe for every Jew, revealing the secret hidden in each one. He then turns to the Jew sold 'le'eiker mishpachas ger', to avodah zarah itself. The Torah insists he must be redeemed, and yovel brings him back to his family even against his will. Following the Baal HaTurim, the nineteen mentions of geulah in the parsha parallel the blessings of Shemoneh Esrei, and the advice for one who has fallen is good friends and attachment to Torah, illustrated by a story. Through Rus, David, Beis Lechem and Kever Rochel he shows where yovel's redemption rests, ending with the secrets of the Torah and of every Jew.

en: Yovel means returning to the root: the fiftieth year, like Shavuos the fiftieth day, brings every Jew back to the place he comes from.
Every Jew carries a hidden secret, a point in which he is greater than everyone, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, a soul of yovel, is the one who reveals it.
A Jew sold to avodah zarah itself, who has reached the point of no return, is not abandoned: the Torah demands his redemption and yovel takes him out.

Following the Baal HaTurim, the nineteen mentions of geulah in the parsha correspond to the blessings of Shemoneh Esrei, with the twelfth, 'le'eiker mishpachas ger', matching the blessing against the heretics.
The remedy for one who has fallen is to attach himself to Torah and to good friends who fear Hashem, as the prophet Malachi says.
Rus, sold as it were to Moav and redeemed back to her root, is read on Shavuos, the day of yovel, and Beis Lechem, place of Kever Rochel and of Moshiach, is the place of yovel.
